outcome: A neutral, resource-bounded benchmark substrate is independently calibrated so later harness comparisons can vary the harness without confounding model, task, environment, evaluator or accounting semantics.
currentProblem: The prior BB-065 objective conflated benchmark calibration with a six-pair Direct-vs-Core product-value study. Recent benchmark research makes that premise stale: provider/termination failure must be separated from independent quality, heterogeneous harnesses need one fixed-factor adapter contract, and substrate validity must be proven before ExHarness value is measured.
constraints: BB-065 establishes benchmark trustworthiness only; it cannot conclude that ExHarness, Direct, Core Sync or any future async profile adds product value.
Research must compare reuse with the smallest ExHarness-owned seam, inspect primary sources and pin selected substrate/version/task identities before READY.

Harness comparisons must fix model snapshot, task/prompt input, starting workspace/environment, resource ceilings, artifact extraction and independent evaluator while preserving each harness's native execution behavior.

Provider, infrastructure and termination state are orthogonal to independent quality. Timeout, 429, UNKNOWN usage or budget exhaustion cannot be silently converted to verifier rejection, and producer success cannot become acceptance.
Every run keeps exact artifact/candidate identity, trace and token/tool/cost/time accounting where known; unknown usage stays explicit and all attempts/retries remain visible.
Calibration is finite and resource-bounded. Real-provider evidence is distinct from deterministic controls; no fabricated live calls, costs, cache hits or judgments.
successCriteria: A pinned task/environment/evaluator substrate has reproducible fresh reset, exact artifact extraction and independent oracle/pass plus no-op/fail controls sufficient to detect invalid or flaky benchmark tasks before harness-value experiments.

A neutral harness adapter contract fixes model, task/prompt, starting workspace/environment, tool/resource ceilings, artifact extraction and evaluator while permitting native harness execution to vary as the experimental factor.

A common run record binds task/environment/harness/model/profile/candidate identities, trace, verifier quality, model/tool usage, cost/time accounting and explicit termination/provider/infrastructure classes; quality remains independent from those failure dimensions and UNKNOWN never becomes zero.

A preregistered calibration/repeat protocol proves the substrate, reset, verifier and accounting paths are executable and hands a pinned benchmark contract to downstream harness-isolation and delivery-value work without making a Direct-vs-ExHarness value claim.
